annotations.text:
Round 4, 3 September
The structure you kept stays: the claim, the eight ailments, a page each, the slip. What changes is the world the site lives in. Four worlds, one hero screen each, same words.
A: a temple morning, garlands, the diya, the motto first. B: the body itself is the front door; touch where it hurts. C: dawn and the daily routine, rounder and warmer. D: Lucknow, the jaali screen and the Awadhi arch.
Also pick a display face on the top board; it is a separate choice.
Judge the world, not the copy. Whichever you pick, I carry it through Home, the ailment pages, the slip, batches, stories, credentials, contact, on phone and desktop, Hindi and English.

Round 3, 3 September
You asked for a theme that comes from what the site is for. This is it: निरामय, free from disease. The visitor picks their illness first; every page speaks to that illness; the slip of practice and the students who had the same thing are the proof; her degree and certificates are the reason to trust.
What to judge: does it feel like hers, and would a person with sugar or a bad back book? Photos are still hatched blocks.
Theme board: the motto, the four ailment families and their colours, the tiles, the slip, the type. Pink and blue survive from round 2 with jobs; kohl takes the footer.
Left: Home on a phone. Middle: what a visitor sees after tapping शुगर. Right: Home on a desktop. Every ailment gets a page like the middle one; that is also what people search for in Hindi.

Round 2, 3 September
Bhagwa is now #FF9933, with dark text on it. Hindi first, with an English switch in the header. The claim is in the site's own words. Indigo is out.
Three things to pick: a logo (D, E or F), a companion colour, and a direction for the whole site (1, 2 or 3). Round 1 is on the page menu.
D. The word योग itself is the mark, in bhagwa, with वंदना beside it. Yoga is literal; every Hindi reader gets it at once; it works at favicon size.
E. A figure with arms raised, drawn in one stroke, beside the Devanagari name. Says yoga to everyone. Trade-off: the most common yoga logo idea.
F. The Devanagari va inside a rising sun: morning practice, saffron dawn. Subtler. Trade-off: read as yoga mainly by people who already practise.
Companion colour: takes the footer, the invite band and small labels. Not blue-indigo, not green. Each card shows the same band, button and tinted card so they compare fairly.

Three directions, same content, same colours, all in Hindi. Judge the personality, not the placeholder photos. The one you pick becomes the full site: every page, phone and desktop, in Hindi and English.
Round 1, 2 September. Kept for reference. Set aside: indigo, the English-first copy, logos A to C.
Round 1 home page. Feedback: too basic, template-driven, no personality. Round 2 answers that.

Final, 3 September, after the marketing and product audit
Added: her face and the Google line under the hero; three steps to start; before/after rows on results and a call to action after them; the 21-day reminder line; four questions on Home; the booking band that builds the WhatsApp message from two rows of chips, with call and form beside it; per-day prices, next-batch dates, family and first-month offer slots; share-to-family links; a page for existing students (fees, class link, holidays, rules); analytics events on every button.
Square brackets are facts to fill. Hatched blocks are photos. Nothing is built yet.
Cards were chosen; the figure stays only for reference.
The plan files in ~/Game/yoga-site match these boards. Next: a session with Opus that reads BUILD-PROMPT.md and EXECUTION-PLAN.md and builds.
